Based on the provided JSON files, I will analyze the strategic options for both the 
United States and Soviet Union following the discovery of Soviet missile bases in 
Cuba.
United States Strategic Options
Option 1: Naval Quarantine/Blockade
Rationale (per JSON): President Kennedy favors this approach as it represents a 
"middle course" that addresses the threat while leaving room to escalate if needed. 
The State Department supports this as it allows for diplomatic pressure while 
avoiding immediate war. • Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet ships approaching quarantine line (confrontation 
decision point) • Probable: OAS/UN diplomatic activity (State Dept seeks multilateral 
support) • Possible: Soviet compliance or defiance at sea
Option 2: Immediate Air Strikes
Rationale (per JSON): The Defense Department/Joint Chiefs strongly advocate this, 
viewing it as the "surest way to neutralize the threat." They believe a blockade 
alone won't compel Soviet withdrawal. • Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet military response (per their defensive readiness 
stance) • Probable: Some missiles survive and become operational • Possible: Soviet retaliation in Berlin or elsewhere

Option 3: Diplomatic Freeze/UN Inspection
Rationale (per JSON): State Department's preferred initial approach - seeking 
"missile standstill under United Nations oversight" before escalation. • Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet diplomatic response (acceptance/rejection) • Probable: Time pressure from military (missiles becoming 
operational) • Possible: Allied pressure for stronger action
Soviet Union Strategic Options
Option 1: Continue Covert Deployment
Rationale (per JSON): Khrushchev's strategy relies on "secrecy and surprise" - continuing deployment while denying presence could buy time to make missiles 
operational. • Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: U.S. public revelation (ending secrecy advantage) • Probable: Increased U.S. surveillance and military preparations
• Possible: Preemptive U.S. military action
Option 2: Defensive Mobilization
Rationale (per JSON): Soviet Armed Forces stance of "hawkish, deterrence-oriented" 
response - elevate alert status and prepare for confrontation. • Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: Increased global tension (Variable: Tension +0.05) • Probable: U.S. military counter-mobilization
• Possible: Accidental escalation from high alert status
Option 3: Private Diplomatic Outreach
Rationale (per JSON): Khrushchev prefers "backchannel and personal diplomacy" - secret negotiations to defuse while maintaining public denial. • Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: U.S. response to overture
• Probable: Internal Soviet debate (Presidium consensus needed) • Possible: Leak undermining Soviet position
Most Plausible Combinations
Primary Path: U.S. Quarantine + Soviet Continued 
Deployment
Logic: This combination reflects each side's dominant preference per JSON - Kennedy's "middle course" and Khrushchev's reliance on "secrecy and surprise." 
Both actions allow flexibility while avoiding immediate military confrontation.
